newsitem.title: GERMANY: FALL IN STERLING FAILS TO STIR GERMAN COCOA BUYERS.
newsitem.headline: FALL IN STERLING FAILS TO STIR GERMAN COCOA BUYERS.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers continue to delay bean and butter purchases because sterling-related savings are being offset by relatively high cocoa prices, traders said on Wednesday.
"Buyers enquired for first quarter beans this morning but found the 3.05 marks/kg on offer was some 0.15 pfennigs above their ideas," one trader said.
"The December futures position is at the higher end of its current trading range and there is no buying incentive."
Third quarter 1997 beans were at 2.96-2.99 marks (3.04 last week) and fourth quarter at 3.01-3.02 (3.11), basis cif good West African quality.
Sterling was at 2.9045 marks at the daily Frankfurt exchange fixing versus 3.0097 marks last week.
Traders said it was hard to disagree with a forecast by an unnamed analyst on Tuesday that the Ivory Coast might produce a broadly unchanged main crop of 1.1 million tonnes in 1997/98.
But they were keenly awaiting reliable information from official bodies on likely shipping patterns and crop quality.
An El Nino weather pattern could bring dry weather to Central and South American growing regions but there were no reports confirming threats to African cocoa areas, they said.
European industry and trade stocks were described as comfortable, with medium-size companies shorter than multinationals at two or three months, but in no hurry to cover.
The cocoa butter ratio over futures was at 2.51 for the third quarter and at 2.49 for the fourth.
Implied butter prices liquid, ex-works, were 7.51 marks (7.60 last week) for the third quarter and 7.56 marks (7.70) for the fourth.
